content.text: That backgrounded container-creation command finally completed after I'd already moved on — let me check whether it left anything behind.

input.description: Check whether the delayed background task created a stray container

content.text: Good — nothing stray was left (grep found no matches; the network was already removed, so the container creation had nowhere to attach and never persisted). Environment is clean. Now let's commit the port-conflict fix.

input.description: Stage the port-conflict fix and its test

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Tear down stale compose-project containers before substrate boot

The pre-substrate-rename portal compose project was never torn down,
so it kept holding host ports 80/443 and made this project's own
caddy container fail to bind them on the #97 deploy — plausibly
interrupting Directus mid-bootstrap, before it seeded the admin user
(#99). Cloud-init now removes any running container whose
com.docker.compose.project label isn't this project's own before
pulling/starting the stack.

Extracted the cloud-init string-templating into a pulumi-free module
(substrate-bootstrap-script.ts) so this is unit testable; verified
the actual cleanup logic by hand against real containers on a local
compose network (a stale differently-labeled container holding a
port gets removed, same-project and unrelated ones don't).

Fixes #99
EOF
)"
